judgments.note: Neighbors' appeal of a DRB approval to build a new single-family house where an approved duplex was never built; constructing a new house is new housing under the guide's table.
Both pre-trial decisions state the appeal is de novo, and the court held a site visit and evidentiary merits hearing and approved the application itself.
Filing date stated explicitly (Sept 9, 2004); Judgment Order of Aug 29, 2007 concludes the appeal with nothing pending shown.
One new house is authorized in place of a never-built approved duplex; counted as 1 newly authorized dwelling. Not a replacement of existing housing, since the duplex was not built.
The house sits on one lot combining the two lots planned for the duplex and the amendment does not modify lot sizes; no new residential lot is created, so 0.
The DRB approved the amendment and granted the requested setback modification; no conditions are quoted, so approved rather than approved_with_conditions.

Three appellants filed; Elizabeth Yates and Marsha Leete later withdrew. Leete's relationship to the property is not stated. Milton Yates represented himself and the other appellants (doc 1), so they are counted as represented.
Milton Yates is pro se (an attorney representing himself); the co-appellants were represented by him per doc 1.

Aesthetic compatibility (Q16) and the setback reduction (Q12) were two of the three questions surviving to trial, but no passage says they were the principal part of the challenge, which originally spanned 67 mostly ownership and prior-approval questions.
The judgment conditions require building per the applicants' own plans and renderings and grant the requested setback modification; no change to the proposal itself is shown.
The Superior Court declaratory action and its Supreme Court appeal (2006-139) are distinct proceedings that stayed this appeal; the Superior Court docket number is not given.

history.note: Labeled from all three decisions: in scope, de novo, approved with conditions after merits hearing.
